openai.sample_unit: patients completing the intervention and postintervention measures

links.outcome: Patient-reported acceptability and appropriateness of chatbot-guided safety planning
links.effect: Self-administered acceptability median 4.00 (3.81-4.56); appropriateness 4.25 (3.75-4.25). Across modalities, H=3.90, P=.14 and H=1.05, P=.59, respectively.
links.quote: Participants rated the acceptability and appropriateness of ReachCare in the ED highly, with no significant difference across the 3 delivery modalities.

unlisted_practices: Self-administered, chatbot-guided suicide safety planning compared with in-person or telehealth clinician delivery.

links.effect: H=0.60, P=.74 comparing chatbot to in-person and telehealth clinicians
links.quote: The safety plans created across all 3 modalities were high-quality (H=0.60, P=.74).

links.effect: median 4.00/5 for both acceptability and appropriateness, with no significant differences across modalities
links.quote: Patients assigned high ratings for the acceptability (median 4.00/5, IQR 4.00-4.50) and appropriateness (median 4.00/5, IQR 4.00-4.25) of ReachCare's ED components, and there were no substantial differences across the 3 delivery modalities [H(acceptability)=3.90, P=.14; H(appropriateness)=1.05, P=.59].
